body.objective: Students will be able to create physical theatre images.
body.iCan: I can create physical theatre images.
successCriteria: I can use my body to create images and environments
I can work with an ensemble to build physical theatre
I can combine physical images with text
body.hook: Imagine a stage with no set: just ten actors. In seconds they become a forest, a speeding train, a storm at sea. Physical theatre uses bodies to create images and tell stories, and it can be more powerful than any painted backdrop.

vocabulary.definition: Theatre that tells stories mainly through the body and movement.

study.title: Bodies as Scenery
study.question: How can actors use bodies to tell a story?
study.passage:
Part 1, Become objects (10 minutes): In groups of five, the teacher calls out an object; groups have 10 seconds to make it with their bodies: a car, a washing machine, a clock, a tree, a bridge.
Part 2, Environments (10 minutes): Create a 3-image sequence showing a place changing:
• A forest at dawn → a storm hits → the forest after the storm
• A city street at rush hour → a power outage → people helping each other
Use levels, focus and slow-motion transitions (count to 8 between images).
Part 3, Add a soundscape (5 minutes): Add sounds with voices and bodies: wind, footsteps, traffic, rain.
Part 4, Add text (15 minutes): Choose a short piece of text, such as a line from a public-domain poem, a proverb, or a line your group writes (for example, "We didn't know how strong we were until the lights went out."). One actor speaks it during the sequence. Decide where it lands for the strongest effect.
Share and feedback: Audience describes what they saw and which image was strongest.
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson.
steps: Add a line of text and perform
discussion: Which object or environment was easiest to create, and why?
How did slow-motion transitions affect the audience?
Where did you place the text, and why there?
How did the soundscape change the mood?
study.product: Write a reflection on your group's physical theatre piece: describe the three images, the transitions, the soundscape and the choice of text placement, and evaluate what was most effective.

examples.title: Levels
examples.problem: How can levels make a forest image stronger?
steps: Some low (roots), some medium (trunks), some high (branches)
examples.answer: Mixing levels creates depth and a full picture

examples.title: Transitions
examples.answer: It keeps the ensemble together and lets the audience follow the change
examples.explore: What would a sudden transition suggest?

examples.title: Soundscape
examples.problem: Create a soundscape for a storm.
examples.answer: Breath for wind, finger taps for rain, stamping for thunder

examples.title: Text placement
examples.problem: Where could a line about strength have the most impact?
examples.answer: During the final image, after the storm or power outage
